newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope says God will never destroy world again.
newsitem.headline: Pope says God will never destroy world again.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Sunday that God would never destroy the world again as the Bible says he did with the Great Flood at the time of Noah.
The Pope made his comments while preaching at a Rome parish before retiring to the Vatican for a week-long Lenten spiritual retreat during which he will make no public appearances.
In his homily the Pope said that after the Great Flood, which the Book of Genesis says was inflicted as punishment for widespread sin in the world, God forged an alliance with Noah.
Noah and his family were the only humans allowed to survive because of their goodness, the Bible says.
"From the words of alliance between God and Noah it is understood that now no sin could bring God to destroy the world he created," the Pope said.

Later, addressing thousands of pilgrims and tourists in St Peter's Square, the Pope asked Catholics to pray, fast and give to the poor during Lent. The 40-day penetential season began last Wednesday and ends on Easter Sunday.
During the week-long spiritual retreat, the Pope and Vatican officials will suspend most official activity while they take part in a programme of prayer and reflection.
